assessment.nobel_worthiness: Surfactant-templated ordered mesoporous silica (MCM-41 family) opened a new class of porous solids with tunable 2-30 nm pores, bridging zeolite chemistry and nanostructured materials. Very high originality and decades of influence on catalysis, adsorption, drug delivery and nanocasting. Structure-property control through design of the architecture is exactly the type of enabling materials chemistry I value.
assessment.attribution: Kresge and Beck led the Mobil discovery (1992) with the liquid-crystal templating mechanism. Ryoo extended it to ordered mesoporous carbons and thicker-walled, more stable silicas through nanocasting. Stucky/Zhao (SBA-15) and Inagaki (FSM-16, earlier folded-sheet route) are also credited; the three-person limit forces exclusion of at least three strong contributors, and the Inagaki priority question complicates a clean Mobil-centred prize.
assessment.maturity: Mature: over thirty years of independent replication, characterization (including electron microscopy and diffraction) and broad application. Recognition is not premature.
uncertainties: Priority between Mobil MCM-41 and the earlier Japanese FSM-16 work is disputed and I cannot verify details independently.
Industrial impact of purely mesoporous silica is more limited than that of zeolites; the prize may be judged as primarily conceptual.
Overlap with the recent MOF/COF prize could make the committee reluctant to honour another porous-materials topic so soon.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Targeted protein degradation via heterobifunctional PROTACs and molecular glues introduced a new pharmacological modality that reprograms the ubiquitin-proteasome system with small molecules. Conceptually original, chemically driven and now in clinical trials, with the structural biology of ternary complexes (crystal structures) explaining selectivity.
assessment.attribution: Crews and Deshaies launched the PROTAC concept (2001) and developed it; Ciulli contributed VHL ligands and ternary-complex structural insight that made the approach drug-like. Handa, Ito and others established the thalidomide/cereblon molecular-glue mechanism, and Sakamoto and Gray also contributed, so the allocation across PROTACs versus glues is unresolved.
assessment.maturity: Rapidly maturing, with many clinical programmes but no approved PROTAC drug as far as I know; the concept is well confirmed mechanistically, but clinical validation is still emerging, so timing could be somewhat early.
uncertainties: I am not certain of the current clinical approval status.
Credit split between PROTAC inventors and the molecular-glue/cereblon discoverers is contentious.
A combined prize may need to omit important contributors.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Cytosine and adenine base editors enable programmable single-nucleotide changes without double-strand breaks, a chemically conceived protein-engineering advance with major therapeutic impact (already in clinical use). Highly original and enabling for the whole community.
assessment.attribution: The decisive contributions are from the Liu laboratory (Komor for cytosine base editors, Gaudelli for adenine base editors, Liu as originator and director). Nishida and Kondo made an independent early cytidine-deaminase fusion, which complicates the credit, but the Liu-lab work is the clearer line.
assessment.maturity: Strongly confirmed and widely adopted, with clinical data emerging; recognition is timely though the CRISPR prize in 2020 may reduce appetite for another genome-editing topic.
uncertainties: Whether the committee views this as a derivative of the 2020 CRISPR prize.
Priority of Nishida/Kondo versus Liu lab on cytidine deaminase editing.
Possible alternative of a Liu-only prize across base and prime editing (B064).

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The crystallographic structure of nitrogenase and the identification of the FeMo-cofactor, including the central light-atom carbide, explain biological nitrogen fixation, one of the most important and difficult reactions in chemistry. The work rests on rigorous structural evidence from X-ray diffraction, which I find compelling.
assessment.attribution: Rees led the first MoFe-protein structure and later cofactor refinement; Einsle resolved the central carbon at atomic resolution; Dean contributed the genetic and biochemical foundation. Ribbe and Seefeldt contributed mechanism and cofactor biochemistry, and the credit among five people is hard to cut to three.
assessment.maturity: Structure is well established and independently confirmed, though the catalytic mechanism of N2 reduction remains incompletely resolved, so recognition would honour structure rather than a complete mechanism.
uncertainties: Mechanism of dinitrogen reduction is still debated.
Allocation between structural biologists and biochemists/geneticists.
Whether the committee prefers to wait for mechanistic closure.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Halide perovskite absorbers transformed photovoltaics, reaching silicon-competitive efficiencies in about a decade from a solution-processed material; the defect tolerance and tunable composition are chemically rich. Very large impact on materials chemistry and energy research.
assessment.attribution: Miyasaka first reported perovskite-sensitized cells (2009), Park and Seok demonstrated the solid-state high-efficiency cell (2012), and Snaith showed the mesosuperstructured and planar high-efficiency devices; Grätzel and Kanatzidis also contributed. The 3-person limit leaves unresolved who is decisive.
assessment.maturity: Scientifically influential but the stability, lead toxicity and commercial deployment questions are not resolved, so recognition may still be premature.
uncertainties: Long-term operational stability and commercial viability remain open.
Many structural details of the perovskite phases and degradation are still under study.
Credit allocation among many contributors is disputed.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Rational design of zeolite and molecular-sieve catalysts with controlled pores and organic structure-directing agents, enabling shape-selective catalysis and new frameworks, including very large-pore and extra-large-pore materials. Industrially significant and close to my own field, where structure determination by electron diffraction has been important.
assessment.attribution: Davis (structure-directing design, large-pore frameworks), Zones (organic structure-directing agents, SSZ materials, Chevron) and Corma (industrial catalysis, ITQ materials) are central; Jihong Yu and Tsapatsis also made major contributions. Credit is broad and diffuse across many frameworks.
assessment.maturity: Very mature, with many decades of use in refining and chemicals, though the field has had less single-moment discovery.
uncertainties: Diffuse credit across a long-running field makes a clear discovery statement difficult.
Possible declared overlap with prior porous-materials prizes.
I have professional proximity to this community and should not overstate my neutrality.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Serial femtosecond crystallography at X-ray free-electron lasers enables structure determination from microcrystals before radiation damage and time-resolved structural dynamics, an enabling method that extended crystallography to previously inaccessible samples. It fits strongly with my appreciation of methods that let a community see what it could not see before.
assessment.attribution: Chapman led the 2011 proof-of-concept work, with Fromme and others on photosystem I nanocrystals, and Schlichting on time-resolved applications; Hajdu conceived the diffraction-before-destruction concept, and the final credit configuration is unclear, particularly if Hajdu is not eligible.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed across multiple facilities, though broad routine use is still limited by beamtime access, so impact is narrower than for synchrotron or cryo-EM methods.
uncertainties: Hajdu's status and whether his credit can be recognized.
Limited accessibility compared with other structural methods.
Impact on chemistry versus structural biology may be perceived as marginal.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: MXenes are a large family of two-dimensional transition-metal carbides and nitrides made by selective etching of MAX phases, with tunable composition and applications in energy storage and electromagnetic shielding. Original inorganic materials chemistry with a clear designed architecture.
assessment.attribution: Naguib, Gogotsi and Barsoum published the first Ti3C2 MXene in 2011, a clearly defined three-person credit with Drexel as the origin.
assessment.maturity: Relatively young, with many applications still at the exploratory stage and few established real-world uses; recognition might be early.
uncertainties: Practical impact beyond laboratory demonstrations is limited.
Structural characterization of surface terminations is still not fully settled.
Age of the field versus the maturity expected by the committee.
